declared.title: Unexpected windfalls, education, and mental health: evidence from lottery winners in Germany
declared.foundIn: counter-evidence report reports/money-happiness/counter-evidence.md; OpenAlex search « unexpected windfalls education and mental health lottery winners Germany » (2026-11-22)

population: German lottery winners observed before and after a large prize, panel data 2000-2011

findings.text: A large windfall does not change the mental health of winners with high education or financial literacy

support.sentence: Unexpected windfalls have no impact on the mental health of individuals with high education or high financial literacy.

findings.text: Winners with low education or low financial literacy see their mental health decline right after the win

support.sentence: Mental health declines immediately after winning a large lottery prize for individuals with low education and low levels of financial literacy.

findings.text: Those same winners say they are happier, while their mental-health scores get worse

support.sentence: While these individuals report being happier after winning the lottery, evidence from commonly used SF-12 measures of mental health indicates that winners with low education experience increased role limitations due to emotional problems, are more anxious, and have less energy after their win.

limits: winners only, before vs after: the comparison group and the panel are not named in the abstract (full text not read)
mental health (SF-12) more than happiness or life satisfaction
